title: African Violet
description: African Violets have round, waxy leaves and small purple flowers 1-2 inches wide. They grow up to 6 inches tall, but are very broad plants spanning up to 12 inches wide.
fun_fact: Although these are called African Violets, they are not closely related to true Violets, which are a completely different plant.
instructions: African Violets should be watered from the base whenever the soil becomes dry, with care taken to not get water on the leaves. They can grow in normal potting soil, and grow better flowers when they are fertilized every other week during the growing season. Make sure to remove the flowers as they die.

title: Aloe
description: Aloe is a very popular succulent plant with thick, fleshy leaves and serrated edges. It can sometimes sprout bright orange or yellow flowers, and can grow to be up to 3 feet tall.
fun_fact: The gel inside of the Aloe leaves is used topically to treat minor skin irritations, but is also eaten in desserts!
instructions: Aloe needs to be watered only when the soil completely dries out, and does not need to be watered at all in the winter. It thrives best in cactus potting mix or some kind of sandy soil. It does not require any fertilizing either. All in all this makes Aloe a very easy plant to care for.

title: Baby Rubber Plant
description: The Baby Rubber Plant is an evergreen perennial with cupped, waxy leaves and small, narrow white flowers. They are typically grown for their beautiful foliage, and are typically 10-12 inches tall.
fun_fact: Although this plant is called the Baby Rubber Plant, it is not truly a rubber plant from which rubber can be made.
instructions: Baby Rubber Plants should be watered every 1-2 weeks in the spring and summer, and let the soil dry out between waterings in the winter. They benefit from misting, and could even make a good bathroom plant to keep that moisture. They need a loose, well-draining potting mix for their soil. Fertilizer once a month during the growing season will help grow more leaves on the plant.

title: Boston Fern
description: The Boston Fern is an evergreen fern typically grows around 1-2 feet tall, with long fronds and small oval leaves along them.
fun_fact: The Boston Fern special mutation of the Nephrolepis Exaltata plant in which its fronds are graceful and arching instead of erect, which gives them a unique look. The name Boston Fern came from the mutation being discovered in a shipment of the plants from Philadelphia to Boston in 1894.
instructions: The soil of the Boston Fern needs to be kept moist with weekly waterings, and also appreciates regular mistings. Boston Ferns grow well in soil with good drainage like a peat-based potting mix. Indoor plants can be fertilized once a month in the spring and summer, and benefit from drastic pruning in order to maintain a great shape.

title: Caladium
description: Caladium has large, heart shaped leaves that are green, white, pink, and red in color. There are also varieties that have lance shaped leaves instead of the heart shaped “fancy leaves.” In houses, they grow to be about 2 feet tall.
fun_fact: The majority of the world’s Caladium fields reside in Florida, where an annual festival is held during the last weekend of July in Lake Placid, Florida.
instructions: Caladiums need to be watered regularly, but don’t need to be watered in the winter when they go dormant and drop their leaves. They grow well in normal potting mix, and should be fertilized every two weeks while they are actively growing. You should trim dying leaves and also any of the flowering spathes in order to get them to grow more of their attractive foliage.

title: Chinese Money Plant
description: The Chinese Money Plant is an evergreen perennial plant with dark green, circular leaves up to wide on long stems. They grow to be up to 12 inches tall.
fun_fact: Native to China, these plants were brought to the western gardening world in the 1940s. Seen as a curiosity for their unique shape, clippings of the Chinese Money Plant were gifted from horticulturist to horticulturist, which earned it the nickname of the “friendship plant.” It didn’t become widely available commercially until the 2010s.
instructions: Chinese Money Plants need to be watered whenever the soil dries out. They should have a moist but well draining soil, and can benefit from monthly fertilizer in the spring and summer. You also need to rotate the plant occasionally to prevent it from becoming lopsided.

title: Fuchsia
description: Fuchsia is a flowering subshrub with long stems and unique flowers which are tubular pendant flowers that come in many shades of red, purple and white.
fun_fact: There are many varieties of Fuchsia for sale, but none are officially recognized with taxonomic status. Most are actually hybrids, which grants them new features.
instructions: Fuchsias need to be kept consistently moist, watered from once a day to a few times a week, and should be misted frequently. They need potting soil with excellent drainage, and should be fertilized every other week in the growing season. You can prune Fuchsias at the beginning of the growing season, and make sure to remove dead flowers to encourage the growth of new ones.

title: Gardenia
description: The Gardenia is a shrub with leathery, dark green leaves and large, white fragrant flowers. As the flowers age, they begin to turn yellow. There are many different cultivars of this plant, each with slightly different attributes.
instructions: Gardenia should be watered weekly, but less frequently in the winter. They may need a humidifier or regular misting to keep them alive if your house is particularly dry, especially in the winter. Gardenias can be grown in normal potting mix, and benefit from being fertilized every three weeks during the growing season to encourage flower growth.

title: Goldfish Plant
description: The Goldfish Plant is a perennial subshrub with small, thick, waxy leaves and bright orange flowers. It grows to be up to 1 foot tall, but can be very wide, spanning up to 3 feet.
fun_fact: The name Goldfish Plant comes from the flower’s resemblance to goldfish!
instructions: Goldfish Plants need to be watered generously in the summer and spring, but a little bit less in the fall and winter. However, at no point should the soil be allowed to dry out completely. A succulent potting mix is perfect for this plant. They should be misted daily, or have a humidifier nearby. Goldfish Plants also need to be fertilized weekly during the growing season.

title: Jade Plant
description: The Jade Plant is a succulent with small pink or white flowers. It has thick branches and thick, shiny leaves that grow in pairs. The flowers grow in clusters and bloom around the wintertime. They are a very popular beginner plant, partly due to the ease of propagation. You can grow a whole new Jade Plant using just one leaf! In their largest form, these plants can be up to 8 feet tall, but most are typically much smaller.
fun_fact: The Jade Plant’s leaves can become tinged with red when grown in direct sunlight.
instructions: Jade Plants are easy to care for. They need to have their soil kept moist with regular watering, with care taken to make sure that the soil does not get soggy. However, in the winter, you only need to water them once a month. They require a loose, well draining soil like succulent potting mix.

title: Laceleaf
description: Laceleaf is a flowering perennial plant that thrives best in tropical climates. It has large, heart shaped leaves to go with smaller, waxy, heart shaped spathes which are bright red. Its beauty is the draw, as this plant is toxic to all mammals, including humans.
fun_fact: The bright red “flower” of Laceleaf is not actually a flower, but instead a spathe, which is a shield-like leaf designed to protect multiple tiny flowers which bloom occasionally.
instructions: Laceleaf should be watered as the soil begins to dry out, keeping the soil slightly moist. It usually ends up needing water once a week indoors. They need a mix of potting soil and orchid mix, and require a trellis to grow properly. They should be fertilized every week to stay healthy and flower. As leaves die, they should be pruned from the plant.

title: Parlor Palm
description: The Parlor Palm is a small palm tree, which is actually the most sold houseplant palm in the world. In households, it grows to be up to 6 feet tall once it has been taken care of for a long time. Although it grows to be large, it starts blooming at a very small size with large clusters of little yellow and orange-red flowers.
fun_fact: The leaves of the Parlor Palm are often harvested to be in flower arrangements.
instructions: Parlor Palms are known as the easiest indoor palm to grow. They should only be watered as the soil begins to be too dry, as they are sensitive to overwatering. They grow well in normal potting soil, and can be fertilized lightly annually to encourage growth.

title: Pepper Plant
description: The Pepper Plant has leafy stems that grow from 6-8 inches, and long, bright, glossy fruits that vary from 1-3 inches. The peppers on this plant are actually edible, although they are known for being very spicy!
fun_fact: This plant is closely related to famous poisons such as deadly nightshade, but also very closely related to commercial foods like bell peppers.
instructions: Pepper Plants need to be kept moist, and watered at least once a week. They grow well in an all-purpose potting mix. To make them flower and fruit properly, they need to be regularly fertilized. They self-pollinate, so will produce peppers without you (or bugs!) having to do more work.

title: Pothos
description: Pothos is an evergreen pine, with beautiful heart shaped leaves. Outdoors, it can grow up to 60 feet tall with 18 inch leaves, however indoors it can grow up to two yards tall indoors with the support of a trellis and the leaves are typically less than 8 inches long.
fun_fact: The last time a cultivated Pothos was recorded to have bloomed on its own without the support of artificial hormone supplements was in 1964! This is due to a genetic impairment in this strain of plant.
instructions: Pothos need to be watered every 1-2 weeks, but the soil should dry out completely between waterings. They can go in normal potting soil, and for more avid growth could use monthly fertilizing in the spring and summer. You can trim these plants to maintain their shape, but otherwise they do not require any pruning.

title: Silver Evergreen
description: The Silver Evergreen’s draw is its large leaves with colors ranging from dark green to light green to even hints of silver. This plant comes in many sizes, and at its largest can be 4 feet tall with 12 inch leaves, but can also be small enough to sit on a table or desk.
fun_fact: Although this plant can flower, many people who keep Silver Evergreens actually cut off the buds as they appear as they are less aesthetically pleasing than the leaves and use a lot of the plant’s energy.
instructions: Silver Evergreens should only be watered as they soil begins to dry out. They grow well in normal potting soil, and can be fertilized at the beginning and end of the growing season. You can prune discolored or dead leaves at their base.

title: Snake Plant
description: The Snake Plant is an evergreen perennial plant with large, thick leaves that grow vertically from a base. In optimal conditions, the plant can grow to be 6ft tall, but they are typically much smaller as houseplants.
fun_fact: The look of the leaves inspired the name “snake plant.” Other common names for this plant include “mother-in-law’s tongue” for the shape and sharpness of its leaves, and the “viper’s bowstring hemp,” because its plant fibers have been used to make bowstrings.
instructions: Snake Plants have a reputation of being a very easy to care for, beginner plant. They need to be watered when the dirt is dry, which is usually once every two weeks. It prefers a loose, well-drained potting soil. It is recommended to fertilize Snake Plants twice a year - once in the spring, and once mid-summer.

title: Spider Plant
description: The Spider Plant is an evergreen perennial flowering plant with long, skinny leaves and small white flowers. It can grow up to 2 feet high, but if you have it as a hanging plant it will grow to be much longer.
fun_fact: Spider Plants are at risk of getting “burnt tips” due to their sensitivity to the fluoride in tap water.
instructions: Spider Plants need to have their soil kept moist with regular watering, with care taken to make sure that the soil does not get soggy. In the winter, they need to be misted frequently. They love humid conditions of around 50-60% in order to grow their best. Spider Plants should be fertilized once a month during the growing season, but not at all during the winter.

title: ZZ Plant
description: The ZZ Plant is a tropical herbaceous perennial plant. The visible branches of this plant are actually pinnately compound leaves, with multiple shiny leaflets on each one. It typically grows to be 18-24 inches tall.
fun_fact: Although this plant is typically green year round, if it is subjected to drought or cold temperatures it actually loses its leaves like plants in the fall.
instructions: With the nickname of the Eternity Plant, ZZ Plants are known for being hard to kill. They only need to be watered when the soil dries out completely, and can survive for months if you forget to do so. They do well with houseplant potting mix.
